title: Rivergate and Passage
premise: Odile Lockridge, a railroad engineer who has spent three years surveying the closed mountain lines of Rivergate, is pulled out of her self-imposed exile when a government survey team vanishes on the pass, leaving their instruments behind and no footprints in the shale. Following the missing team's route, she uncovers a scheme by the regional administrator Corvus Hale to erase an entire valley settlement from official maps so its water rights can be quietly reassigned. Guided by Tamsin, a girl whose memory of the vanished town is the last living record of it, Odile races the dry season's end across the range to reach the capital archive before winter seals the pass. She arrives with the original alignment charts that prove the town existed, Hale falls to an inquiry he cannot map his way out of, and Odile finally begins measuring life in years again.
about_author: Vesper Underhill is the pen name of a former track inspector who walked more abandoned rail miles than paved ones before turning to fiction. They write from a converted signal box overlooking a river they refuse to name.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Establishes her solitary routine surveying closed lines around Rivergate, measuring distance instead of time since her brother's death. When she finds an unmarked government cache of survey gear abandoned on the old spur, the emotional beat is unease: someone was here, and left in a hurry.

chapters.title: The Team That Left No Tracks
chapters.summary: Odile follows the gear trail up the shale slopes and finds the survey team's camp intact but empty—boots, ledgers, cold stove. No tracks lead out. POV shifts briefly to a recovered journal entry from team leader Anselm Reeve. Beat: dread sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Wouldn't Say
chapters.summary: Back at her cabin, Odile decodes Reeve's ledger: elevation readings for a valley officially listed as uninhabited, yet noting fences, orchards, a schoolhouse bell. Flashback to her brother's disappearance on these same lines. Beat: grief braided with suspicion.

chapters.title: Corvus Hale Signs the Papers
chapters.summary: Antagonist POV. Administrator Hale reviews the vanished team's reports and orders the valley's records 'consolidated.' His calm bureaucratic menace contrasts Odile's rough honesty. Beat: the reader sees the machinery of erasure begin turning.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Remembers Bellbrook
chapters.summary: Odile encounters Tamsin, a feral-capable teenager living off the line, who claims to have been born in Bellbrook—a town that appears on no map. Her memories are vivid, specific, impossible. Beat: wonder; Odile's cynicism cracks.

chapters.title: Closed Lines, Open Wounds
chapters.summary: Odile tests Tamsin's memory against her own surveys: every landmark matches terrain she has measured but never questioned. Realization lands—the maps were altered, not the land. Beat: vertigo of discovering reality itself was doctored.

chapters.title: Hale's Men on the Spur
chapters.summary: Hale's enforcer Dree and her crew arrive at Odile's cabin, confiscating papers and warning her off the high country. Odile hides the ledger in a culvert. Beat: fear converting to defiance; invisibility is over.

chapters.title: The Dry Season Clock
chapters.summary: Odile calculates: eleven days until autumn rains close the pass, then snow. The only route to the capital archive runs through the range ahead of the weather. She decides to go. Tamsin insists on coming. Beat: commitment; the adventure proper begins.

chapters.title: Water Over Rails
chapters.summary: The pair crosses a flooded cutting where the river has reclaimed the trackbed. Odile's engineering knowledge saves them; Tamsin's knowledge of pre-erasure paths saves them again. Beat: trust forming between two kinds of memory—measured and lived.

chapters.title: Dree Closes the Gap
chapters.summary: Dree's POV. She tracks the fugitives, motivated less by loyalty than by her own erased past—she was Bellbrook's constable and chose to forget. Beat: antagonist complexity; pursuit tightens.

chapters.title: The Tunnel Under the Shoulder
chapters.summary: A collapsed tunnel forces a dangerous traverse through its black interior. Odile relives her brother's final hours in flashback; Tamsin anchors her with the bell song of Bellbrook. Beat: catharsis through shared darkness.

chapters.title: Anselm Reeve, Alive
chapters.summary: They find Reeve hiding in a maintenance hut above the snowline, injured, the sole survivor. He reveals Hale ordered the team silenced after they found Bellbrook's original charter sealed in the rock. Beat: confirmation; stakes become mortal.

chapters.title: What Hale Erased First
chapters.summary: Reeve explains the pattern: Bellbrook is not the first town Hale has unmapped—there were four others, each dissolved into administrative silence. Odile realizes the archive holds the proof only if it still exists. Beat: scale of corruption revealed.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Weir
chapters.summary: Reeve, terrified, tries to bargain with Dree's crew by radio, trading Odile's location for extraction. Tamsin overhears. The group fractures. Beat: betrayal; lowest point of trust.

chapters.title: Splitting the Range
chapters.summary: Odile sends Reeve down one path as decoy and takes the high traverse with Tamsin toward the capital. Storm clouds gather early. Beat: sacrifice and strategy; tension ratchets.

chapters.title: The Archive Burns Early
chapters.summary: Capital POV interlude: Hale, learning Reeve survived, orders a 'records fire' at the provincial archive. Odile watches smoke rise from the pass road. Beat: despair—the goal may already be ash.

chapters.title: Tamsin's Testimony
chapters.summary: Tamsin reveals she isn't just a survivor—she copied Bellbrook's charter as a child, memorized it whole, and recites it to Odile through the storm night. Memory itself becomes the document. Beat: theme crystallizes; hope rekindled.

chapters.title: Snowline Standoff
chapters.summary: Dree corners them at the last shelter below the pass. But seeing Tamsin recite the charter, Dree remembers her own erased oath as Bellbrook's constable—and turns her weapon on her own crew. Beat: climax pivot; justice outside the law.

chapters.title: Over the Pass Before the Snows
chapters.summary: Odile, Tamsin, and a wounded Dree cross the summit in the season's first blizzard, navigating by Odile's hand-drawn alignments when all else fails. Beat: triumph earned through craft and endurance.

chapters.title: The Inquiry at Rivergate Hall
chapters.summary: In the capital, Odile presents her surveys against the falsified maps; Tamsin recites the charter before the inquiry board; Dree testifies. Hale's careful paper world collapses under measured fact and remembered word. Beat: legal climax; power confronted.

chapters.title: Bellbrook Back on the Map
chapters.summary: Weeks later, surveyors restore Bellbrook to the rolls. Survivors trickle home; Tamsin chooses to stay with Odile rather than return alone. Beat: restoration, bittersweet—what was lost cannot fully return.

chapters.title: Years, Not Miles
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, closing frame. Spring on the reopened line; she plants a marker at her brother's stretch of track and lets herself count seasons now instead of miles. Final beat: memory honored, exile ended, the journey inward complete.
